tier1.text: A large organ beneath the right side of the diaphragm. It processes absorbed nutrients, produces bile, and synthesizes many proteins carried in the blood.
tier1.attribution: Text from Human Atlas by ashemag (github.com/ashemag/human-atlas), MIT License

tier2.text: The liver, the largest internal organ in humans, plays a key part in digesting fats by making bile, a digestive juice needed to break down the fat in food. As the body's chemical processing plant, the liver also packages nutrients from digestion, makes proteins carried in the blood, and gets rid of worn-out cell parts and wastes. Protected by the surrounding ribs, the liver lies in the upper right part of the abdomen, below the diaphragm, the dome-shaped muscle under the lungs. Two main parts, or lobes, make up the liver: a large right lobe and a much smaller left lobe. Blood reaches the liver through the hepatic artery, which brings oxygen-rich blood from the heart, and through the hepatic portal vein, which brings nutrients absorbed from the small intestine. The liver controls how these nutrients are distributed to the rest of the body and removes toxic substances, such as drugs and alcohol. The liver's working units are lobules, where blood flows from the edge of each lobule to a central vein through open, porous blood spaces called sinusoids. Hepatocytes, the liver's main cells, are packed tightly around the sinusoids and process the nutrients, toxins and wastes carried by the blood. The sinusoids also contain star-shaped Kupffer cells, which remove dead red and white blood cells, bacteria and other foreign material that enter the sinusoids. Bile made by hepatocytes collects in bile canaliculi, small ducts between the hepatocytes, and then flows through larger ducts that join and leave the liver as the common hepatic duct.

sentences.text: The liver, the largest internal organ in humans, plays a key part in digesting fats by making bile, a digestive juice needed to break down the fat in food.

quotes.quote: The liver is the largest internal organ in humans and it plays a very important role in digestion of fats and detoxifying blood. The liver produces bile, a digestive juice that is required for the breakdown of fatty components of the food in the duodenum.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: As the body's chemical processing plant, the liver also packages nutrients from digestion, makes proteins carried in the blood, and gets rid of worn-out cell parts and wastes.

quotes.quote: The liver is a complex biochemical processing plant. It packages nutrients absorbed by the digestive system; produces plasma proteins, clotting factors, and bile; and disposes of worn-out cell components and waste products.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Protected by the surrounding ribs, the liver lies in the upper right part of the abdomen, below the diaphragm, the dome-shaped muscle under the lungs.

quotes.quote: The liver lies inferior to the diaphragm in the right upper quadrant of the abdominal cavity and receives protection from the surrounding ribs.
quotes.section: 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: the hepatic artery delivers oxygenated blood from the heart to the liver. The hepatic portal vein delivers partially deoxygenated blood containing nutrients absorbed from the small intestine
quotes.section: 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder

sentences.text: The liver controls how these nutrients are distributed to the rest of the body and removes toxic substances, such as drugs and alcohol.

quotes.quote: Absorbed nutrients in the blood are carried into the hepatic portal vein, which leads to the liver. There, the liver regulates the distribution of nutrients to the rest of the body and removes toxic substances, including drugs, alcohol, and some pathogens.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The liver's working units are lobules, where blood flows from the edge of each lobule to a central vein through open, porous blood spaces called sinusoids.

quotes.quote: The functional units of the liver are lobules with sinusoids that carry blood from the periphery to the central vein of the lobule.
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Accessory Organs. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

quotes.quote: A hepatic sinusoid is an open, porous blood space formed by fenestrated capillaries from nutrient-rich hepatic portal veins and oxygen-rich hepatic arteries.
quotes.section: 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Hepatocytes, the liver's main cells, are packed tightly around the sinusoids and process the nutrients, toxins and wastes carried by the blood.

quotes.quote: Hepatocytes are tightly packed around the fenestrated endothelium of these spaces, giving them easy access to the blood. From their central position, hepatocytes process the nutrients, toxins, and waste materials carried by the blood.
quotes.section: 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: A hepatocyte is the liver’s main cell type, accounting for around 80 percent of the liver's volume.
quotes.section: 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The sinusoids also contain star-shaped Kupffer cells, which remove dead red and white blood cells, bacteria and other foreign material that enter the sinusoids.

quotes.quote: The hepatic sinusoids also contain star-shaped reticuloendothelial cells (Kupffer cells), phagocytes that remove dead red and white blood cells, bacteria, and other foreign material that enter the sinusoids.

quotes.quote: These small ducts accumulate the bile produced by hepatocytes. From here, bile flows first into bile ductules and then into bile ducts. The bile ducts unite to form the larger right and left hepatic ducts, which themselves merge and exit the liver as the common hepatic duct.
quotes.section: 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder
